grammar-empty.stimulus: Hear a complete sentence context with one grammatical slot: The dogs ___ running.
grammar-empty.response: Say the missing word; retain the subject and sentence context through item conversion.
grammar-empty.visibility: Hide the completed sentence and answer word until feedback. A pictured subject may remain visible.
grammar-empty.feedback: Replay The dogs are running, explain the plural subject, then offer a fresh singular/plural contrast.
grammar-empty.score: Judge agreement in this sentence, not an isolated noun. Zero usable items must fail generation validation.

riddle-cues.stimulus: Hear/read: I shine bright in the sky during the day and keep you warm. What am I? Show a neutral question mark.
riddle-cues.response: Say the inferred answer from the clues.
riddle-cues.visibility: Mask the answer symbol, label and accessible answer text throughout the independent attempt. Picture naming keeps its picture visible under a different stimulus contract.
riddle-cues.feedback: After a correct answer or explicit teaching reveal, show the sun and connect it to the clues. A revealed answer is assisted; use a fresh riddle for an independent retry.
riddle-cues.score: Accept defensible clue-consistent answers. Verify the learner cannot identify the answer from the picture, alt text or tutor cue before responding.
riddle-cues.liveCheck: Clue-only attempt, reveal and fresh retry

picture-stimulus.stimulus: Show an actual pillow picture, not the string pillows in a picture field.
picture-stimulus.response: Say a defensible related object in the existing association mode.
picture-stimulus.visibility: Keep the base picture visible; hide the example partner answer until feedback.
picture-stimulus.feedback: Explain the relationship to an accepted partner; do not replace invalid generated pictures with guessed answers.
picture-stimulus.score: Validate image/emoji stimuli before retaining an item. This repair alone does not satisfy a visual-card matching requirement.

picture-matching.stimulus: Show two picture sets: sock/spoon and shoe/fork, with shuffled partner positions.
picture-matching.response: Connect or tap a pair of related pictures; use separate task identities for opposites, location or morphology.
picture-matching.visibility: Both sets stay visible. Hide correct links, partner highlights and answer-revealing labels until submission.
picture-matching.feedback: Show the chosen relationship and explain a mismatch before allowing a new match.
picture-matching.score: Score the actual pair selected; allow all defensible pairs and reject ambiguous stimulus sets.

k-grammar-completion.stimulus: Hear I see ___ apple or a pronoun/tense context that determines the missing form.
k-grammar-completion.response: Produce the missing grammatical form aloud; sentence creation is a separate response contract.
k-grammar-completion.visibility: Expose needed context but hide the completed form. Do not require independent reading.
k-grammar-completion.feedback: Model the full sentence after the attempt and contrast the relevant form.
k-grammar-completion.score: Use context-sensitive accepted forms; distinguish an article, agreement, pronoun and tense trial.

k-sentence-builder.stimulus: Show a scene and shuffled pictured word tiles with individual audio, such as dog / runs / The.
k-sentence-builder.response: Arrange tiles into a sentence and submit the ordered sequence.
k-sentence-builder.visibility: Tile words and audio are available; hide the assembled model sentence until feedback.
k-sentence-builder.feedback: Read back the submitted construction, identify its issue and support revision.
k-sentence-builder.score: Judge valid sentence structures, meaning and the requested punctuation. Tile assembly does not prove handwriting or spontaneous speech.

letter-writing.stimulus: Trace: letter path on the writing surface. Copy: model beside a blank surface. Write: spoken letter name with a blank surface.
letter-writing.response: Draw ordered strokes with pointer, touch or stylus; capture paths and pen lifts.
letter-writing.visibility: Trace shows the path; copy removes the overlay but retains the side model; independent write hides the letter form and arrows until feedback.
letter-writing.feedback: Overlay submitted strokes against the reference after submission. Offer a supported trace separately from an independent reattempt.
letter-writing.score: Assess path coverage, formation and required stroke sequence with age-appropriate tolerances. Keep trace/copy/write outcomes separate and preserve cumulative letter groups and case.
letter-writing.liveCheck: Stroke capture, pen lifts, clear and resubmit
letter-writing.reuseFinding: Both existing LetterTracing components display letters/guides only: neither captures drawing input nor scores strokes. Reuse display ideas and inspect number/shape tracing infrastructure for capture; interactive letter formation still needs implementation.

print-concepts.stimulus: Use a real rendered book page, contents page or line of print.
print-concepts.response: Point to a word/space/feature, track reading direction, count words or navigate to a named section as required.
print-concepts.visibility: Keep print visible; hide target highlighting and navigation answers until the learner acts.
print-concepts.feedback: Highlight the relevant print unit or show the correct route on the same page.
print-concepts.score: Judge the selected region, tracking path, count or destination separately; page-feature recognition alone is insufficient.

sound-production.stimulus: Present the required word or letter with audio appropriate to the exact objective; separate phonemes, onset/rime and syllables.
sound-production.response: Produce the specified sound or sequence of chunks; a count or menu selection is separate recognition evidence.
sound-production.visibility: Do not model the requested answer sounds before the independent attempt. Letter visibility depends on whether correspondence is being assessed.
sound-production.feedback: Model the exact sound/chunks after the attempt and label imitation as assisted practice.
sound-production.score: Define judgeable sounds and exclusions per requirement. Retain teacher-reviewable audio where automatic isolated-sound judging is unreliable.
sound-production.liveCheck: Sound capture and per-sound judge limits

ending-sounds.stimulus: Hear words with controlled final-phoneme contrasts, for example cap and cat.
ending-sounds.response: Choose the matching ending sound or produce it in an explicitly separate production task.
ending-sounds.visibility: Hide printed endings for auditory assessment; ensure onset pictures cannot determine the correct choice.
ending-sounds.feedback: Replay and emphasize final sounds after the choice.
ending-sounds.score: Score final-phoneme evidence, not whole-word rhyme or initial-sound matching.

syllable-blending.stimulus: Play cow + boy as two syllables, or c + at as onset and rime, without decomposing the requested chunks.
syllable-blending.visibility: Hide the whole-word label and identifying answer picture before the response.
syllable-blending.feedback: Join the original chunks and reveal the word after the attempt.
syllable-blending.score: Judge the whole word while validating that the audio preserves the objective's chunk boundaries.
syllable-blending.liveCheck: Chunk audio timing and spoken blend

vowel-contrast.stimulus: Play a controlled short/long vowel contrast such as cap/cape with equivalent contextual support.
vowel-contrast.response: Choose the heard vowel contrast or produce the requested vowel in a separate task.
vowel-contrast.visibility: Hide spelling cues when testing auditory discrimination; show orthography only for an explicit print-to-sound task.
vowel-contrast.feedback: Replay the contrasting vowels and then connect sound to print if relevant.
vowel-contrast.score: Require vowel-specific evidence; silent-e recognition must not stand in for listening discrimination.

extended-decoding.stimulus: Show an in-scope inflected or compound word, with sentence context only when required.
extended-decoding.response: Read it aloud; answer a separate meaning question where the objective includes comprehension.
extended-decoding.visibility: Keep print visible but withhold tutor pronunciation and answer-identifying pictures before cold reading.
extended-decoding.feedback: Model decoding after the attempt, then use a new word to check independent transfer.
extended-decoding.score: Validate phonics scope and score decoding separately from word meaning.
extended-decoding.liveCheck: Cold reading and separate meaning response

oral-interaction.stimulus: Present a bounded conversation with missing information, such as an unclear direction the child needs to clarify.
oral-interaction.response: Ask an original relevant question and respond to the partner's next turn.
oral-interaction.visibility: Do not supply the exact question as a script to repeat; retain contextual pictures if needed.
oral-interaction.feedback: Respond to the child's actual question and discuss relevance or turn-taking after the exchange.
oral-interaction.score: Retain turn-level audio and rubric evidence; use teacher observation for behaviors the system cannot observe.

oral-sentence-production.stimulus: Show a meaningful scene or target vocabulary and ask the child to describe it.
oral-sentence-production.response: Produce an original sentence using the required concept or structure.
oral-sentence-production.visibility: Keep the scene visible; hide model sentences until feedback.
oral-sentence-production.feedback: Acknowledge meaning, then model or prompt revision of the specific missing structure.
oral-sentence-production.score: Accept multiple valid sentences; distinguish a fragment, irrelevant sentence and successful concept use.
oral-sentence-production.liveCheck: Open utterance capture and rubric judgment

oral-storytelling.stimulus: Offer a three-event picture plan or a story to retell, depending on the requirement.
oral-storytelling.response: Record connected original language across the events.
oral-storytelling.visibility: Keep planning pictures available; hide a scripted model retelling during independent production.
oral-storytelling.feedback: Replay the child's narration and identify missing sequence links without replacing creative choices.
oral-storytelling.score: Separate sequence, connected language and source fidelity; retain audio for review.

picture-context.stimulus: Show a contextual scene and read the sentence or story containing the unfamiliar word.
picture-context.response: Explain or select the meaning using details from the supplied context.
picture-context.visibility: Keep useful scene clues visible; avoid a lone answer icon that turns inference into naming.
picture-context.feedback: Point back to the particular picture/text details that support the interpretation.
picture-context.score: Require context-consistent meaning, with a distinct evidence response when the objective asks for it.

two-story-compare.stimulus: Read two short stories with distinct accessible picture references.
two-story-compare.response: Compare a character/event/detail across both, using speech or pictured same/different choices.
two-story-compare.visibility: Retain references to both stories; hide the completed comparison.
two-story-compare.feedback: Show the relevant evidence from each story side by side.
two-story-compare.score: Accept defensible comparisons grounded in both texts; referencing only one is incomplete.

semantic-web.stimulus: Offer picture nodes for a theme or logical chain with unrelated distractors.
semantic-web.response: Connect related nodes and explain the chosen relationship when requested.
semantic-web.visibility: Show the nodes; hide the completed network and relationship labels until submission.
semantic-web.feedback: Discuss individual links and allow revision without imposing one arbitrary network.
semantic-web.score: Judge defensible relations and explanations; accept multiple valid webs.

spatial-expression.stimulus: Show objects in a scene with a fixed, unambiguous viewpoint.
spatial-expression.response: Describe the required relation aloud; object placement remains a separate response type.
spatial-expression.visibility: Keep the scene visible but hide its target relation label before the answer.
spatial-expression.feedback: Highlight the two reference objects and model their spatial relation.
spatial-expression.score: Judge relation and reference object; confirm left/right and front/behind are visually representable.

spatial-paths.stimulus: Show a traversable scene with distinct over, under, through or around routes.
spatial-paths.response: Choose or draw the requested route and animate the object along it.
spatial-paths.visibility: Keep obstacles and routes visible; hide the correct-route highlight until submission.
spatial-paths.feedback: Replay the selected path and contrast the requested movement relation.
spatial-paths.score: Score path geometry or route identity, not merely the final destination cell.
spatial-paths.liveCheck: Route selection, animation and path scoring

picture-sorting.stimulus: Show recognizable pictures of people, places, things or quantities, with accessible category cues.
picture-sorting.response: Move cards into buckets when sorting cards is required; retain spoken categorization as a separate partial capability.
picture-sorting.visibility: Pictures and bucket cues stay visible; hide item-specific correct categories.
picture-sorting.feedback: Return a misplaced card with a category-specific explanation.
picture-sorting.score: Check actual bucket assignments and balanced requested categories, including places where specified.
picture-sorting.liveCheck: Picture recognition, card movement and retry

sort-explanation.stimulus: Retain the sorted item and selected category after categorization.
sort-explanation.response: Explain why this item belongs in that category.
sort-explanation.visibility: Show the child's categorization; withhold a model explanation until the rationale attempt.
sort-explanation.feedback: Connect a valid distinguishing feature to the selected category.
sort-explanation.score: Score the rationale separately; a correct category with an unrelated explanation is not full coverage.

main-idea-organizer.stimulus: Read a story and show a central-idea slot plus pictured detail cards, including related but unstated distractors.
main-idea-organizer.response: Choose a main idea and connect supporting details to it.
main-idea-organizer.visibility: Keep story references available; hide the completed web and correct-detail markers.
main-idea-organizer.feedback: Link each accepted detail to its actual story evidence.
main-idea-organizer.score: Separate main-idea choice from support links; topical similarity alone is insufficient.

story-reasoning.stimulus: Pause a story before the outcome and ask for a prediction and its supporting clue.
story-reasoning.response: Predict an outcome or explain a cause using the information available at that point.
story-reasoning.visibility: Hide future text, outcome images, captions and tutor spoilers until the response is captured.
story-reasoning.feedback: Reveal the outcome and compare it with the child's reasoning without treating every differing prediction as wrong.
story-reasoning.score: Judge plausibility and cited evidence using pre-reveal context; separate prediction quality from matching the author.
story-reasoning.liveCheck: Story reveal timing and reasoning capture

picture-story-sequence.stimulus: Read a short story and show three or four shuffled event pictures with optional audio.
picture-story-sequence.response: Order event cards and identify beginning, middle and end.
picture-story-sequence.visibility: Keep the event pictures visible; hide sequence numbers and the completed order.
picture-story-sequence.feedback: Replay the submitted order against the story and support moving a misplaced event.
picture-story-sequence.score: Score event ordering against the supplied story; avoid relying on print decoding.

multiple-meanings.stimulus: Present two scenes for one word, such as a flying bat and a baseball bat, with separate sentence contexts.
multiple-meanings.response: Select or explain the meaning that fits each context.
multiple-meanings.visibility: Show both senses as legitimate options; hide the correct context-to-sense links.
multiple-meanings.feedback: Compare how the same word refers to different things in the two sentences.
multiple-meanings.score: Judge meaning per context; an isolated vocabulary label does not establish multiple meanings.

rhyme-family.stimulus: Hear a base word and see three empty collection slots.
rhyme-family.response: Produce three distinct rhyming words aloud.
rhyme-family.visibility: Show previously accepted responses to prevent duplicates; hide unused example answers.
rhyme-family.feedback: Celebrate valid new rhymes and explain duplicates or non-rhymes without exhausting the remaining answer pool.
rhyme-family.score: Validate rhyme and uniqueness; accept valid words beyond a fixed exemplar list.
rhyme-family.liveCheck: Repeated spoken collection and duplicate handling

emotion-scenes.stimulus: Show a readable face and situation with enough context to support an emotion inference.
emotion-scenes.response: Name or explain a plausible emotion, depending on the requirement.
emotion-scenes.visibility: Keep facial and scene clues visible; hide emotion labels before the response.
emotion-scenes.feedback: Connect the interpretation to facial or situational cues while acknowledging plausible alternatives.
emotion-scenes.score: Accept supported near-synonyms and alternatives; reject ambiguous stimuli rather than forcing one label.

listening-presentation.stimulus: Play one shared short presentation containing at least three distinct factual details.
listening-presentation.response: Answer three independent recall questions about that same presentation.
listening-presentation.visibility: Withhold answer-bearing transcripts and avoid feedback that supplies answers to later questions; control replay according to the objective.
listening-presentation.feedback: Review source excerpts after the affected independent questions have been attempted.
listening-presentation.score: Link each answer to a different supplied detail and track any replay or assistance.
listening-presentation.liveCheck: Shared audio, recall questions and feedback order

curriculum-clarity.stimulus: Undetermined: the published requirement needs a concrete observable task before stimulus design.
curriculum-clarity.response: Specify what the child must say, select, arrange, draw or write; retain the original objective as provenance.
curriculum-clarity.visibility: Decide which clues are legitimate support only after the assessed action is defined.
curriculum-clarity.feedback: Define one successful example and one near-miss before implementing feedback.
curriculum-clarity.score: Resolve the observable evidence with curriculum review; do not invent a pass criterion and report the requirement as covered.
curriculum-clarity.liveCheck: Blocked on an observable task definition
